headline: Bush Plane Coordination and Backcountry Registration Essentials
reservation: There is no road connection to Lake Clark; arrange suitable air or boat access and lodging in advance. NPS does not require a permit or reservation for ordinary backcountry camping, and registration is voluntary. Follow applicable bear-resistant food-storage requirements; the two public-use cabins require reservations.

days.title: Port Alsworth Arrival and Forest Hiking
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Kenai Municipal Airport

stops.name: Port Alsworth
stops.detail: Land on the gravel airstrip of this lakeside community, the park's primary gateway and hub.

stops.name: Tanalian Falls
stops.detail: Hike the 4-mile round trip trail through birch forest to reach the basalt-cleft waterfall.

days.driving: Walking only within Port Alsworth; flight time is approximately 45 minutes
days.note: Pack all food in and all trash out; there are no municipal disposal services.

days.title: Alpine Lakes and High Country

stops.name: Kontrashibuna Lake
stops.detail: Continue past the falls to the shore of this glacial lake for views of the Aleutian Range.

stops.name: Tanalian Mountain
stops.detail: For those seeking elevation, the steep trail offers a vantage point over the turquoise waters of Lake Clark.

days.driving: Walking only; allow a full day for the mountain ascent
days.note: Mountain weather changes rapidly; carry layers even if the valley is warm.

days.title: Coastal Bear Viewing or Maritime History

stops.name: Dick Proenneke Cabin
stops.detail: Arrange a floatplane charter to Upper Twin Lake to see the hand-built home of the famous naturalist.

stops.name: Silver Salmon Creek
stops.detail: Consider a coastal flight for brown bear viewing in the meadows along Cook Inlet.

days.driving: Air charter only; conditions vary heavily based on wind and visibility
days.note: Proenneke Cabin access is highly weather-dependent and requires a specialized floatplane landing.

intel.title: Air Gateway Logistics
intel.text: Parking for your trip is handled at your departure airport in Anchorage or Kenai. There are no public roads or parking lots for private vehicles within the national park.

intel.title: Satellite Communication
intel.text: Cellular service is virtually non-existent throughout the park. Visitors are encouraged to carry a satellite messenger and download all maps for offline use.

intel.title: Logistical Self-Sufficiency
intel.text: There are no gas stations or large grocery stores in Port Alsworth. All fuel for camp stoves and food must be purchased at your gateway city and flown in.

intel.title: Weather Buffers
intel.text: Flight delays due to fog or wind are common in the Alaska Range. Allow at least one full 'buffer day' in your itinerary to ensure you don't miss onward connections.

intel.title: Charter Requirements
intel.text: Access to remote areas like Twin Lakes or Chinitna Bay requires hiring an FAA-authorized air taxi. Verify your pilot's credentials and current park commercial permits.

plan.arrival: Fly from Anchorage to Kenai or Port Alsworth; ensure all gear is in soft-sided duffels for bush plane weight limits before checking into your lodge.
plan.vehicle: No cars or RVs; transit is limited to bush planes, boats, and walking. Check air taxi weight restrictions for all gear.
plan.goldenHour: Kontrashibuna Lake shore, with a seasonal caveat for the late-night sun during the Alaskan summer.
